19000073_1.STATUS: RECLASSIFIED. v1 called this a comparison limit. It is an ENGINE SUPPORT GAP.
19000073_1.boundary: Manectric Thunderbolt into Linoone (maxhp 261), then Linoone Belly Drum
19000073_1.showdown: Thunderbolt -127 leaves 134/261; Belly Drum then costs 130, leaving 4/261, and sets atk to +6
19000073_1.engine_84pct: move=-135 only. No Belly Drum damage, no boost.
19000073_1.the_gates_are_faithful: Showdown data/moves.ts:1223 refuses when target.hp <= maxhp/2; the engine gen3/choice_effects.rs:642-650 fires when attacker.hp > maxhp/2 with INTEGER division. Identical on both parities: for maxhp = 2k both fire at hp > k; for maxhp = 2k+1 Showdown fires at hp > k+0.5 i.e. hp >= k+1, and the engine's integer maxhp/2 = k fires at hp > k i.e. hp >= k+1. Damage agrees too -- directDamage floors via clampIntRange, so 130.5 -> 130 = the engine's 261/2. The per-roll simulation is CORRECT.
19000073_1.showdown_predicate_is_wider_than_v1_quot: moves.ts:1223 is `target.hp <= target.maxhp/2 || target.boosts.atk >= 6 || target.maxhp === 1`. The engine implements NEITHER of the other two disjuncts: at atk +6 above half HP it still pays maxhp/2 and pushes a Boost of amount 0 (Showdown refuses outright); at maxhp == 1 it fires with damage 0 (Showdown's Shedinja clause refuses). Neither rejects this row, but v1 elided two thirds of the predicate on the line it cited, and both are separate latent engine bugs.
19000073_1.v1s_FALSE_PREMISE: v1 said 'without branch_on_damage the engine offers one representative non-crit roll'. branch_on_damage IS ON. engine_transition_differential.py:1824-1826 and scripts/replay_residue.py:118 both pass True. The realised roll is absent for a different reason entirely.
19000073_1.the_real_cause: the 16-roll preservation this row needs already exists and Belly Drum is simply not on its allowlist. generate_instructions.rs:2911-2915 keeps all sixteen gen3 rolls when branch_on_damage && choice.first_move && pending_hp_reading_move(defender_choice) && fixed_damage.is_none(). pending_hp_reading_move at :1379-1384 is `FLAIL | REVERSAL | SUBSTITUTE`. Thunderbolt moves first and Belly Drum is the defender_choice, so the gate would fire -- BELLYDRUM is just missing from the enum.
19000073_1.the_precedent_is_exact: third_party/poke-engine-gen3-substitute-hp-gate.patch added SUBSTITUTE to that same allowlist for the same reason: gen3 refuses Substitute below a quarter of max, so a roll range straddling the quarter decides whether it happens at all, and collapsing to a representative drops one side from the support. Substitute's gate is maxhp/4 (choice_effects.rs:871); Belly Drum's is maxhp/2 (:645). Same class, already adjudicated once as an ENGINE defect and fixed by an ENGINE patch.
19000073_1.why_v1s_label_was_the_charter_failure: the charter defines a comparison limit as one no same-transition partition can reach -- permanent -- and an engine gap as the support lacking a transition the sim can reach. A partition reaches this; the realised roll 127 = floor(146*87/100) is legal and absent from the support. v1 also used limit:roll_divergent_lethality as its shape precedent, which the charter names as one of three adjudications that turned out to rest on incomplete branch support. It was re-running the exact failure mode, citing the canonical instance of it as warrant.

disposition.gate: needs a tactics-suite regression gate and a single-variable re-sweep reporting matched and skip alongside diverged, per the rules in PR #1038.
disposition.expected_cost: widening the allowlist multiplies branch counts on affected boundaries; that cost must be measured, not assumed negligible.

19000073_1.allowlist_completeness_is_OPEN: pending_hp_reading_move is an enumeration and has now been found short twice. Endeavor (damage = target.hp - user.hp) and Pain Split (averages both HPs) also read the user's HP after a first-mover hit. Adding BELLYDRUM does NOT close the class; it closes one row. Recorded as an open question.
19000073_1.rank_and_prediction: not yet ranked by the charter's search-impact formula, and no class-split prediction with a stated ceiling was pre-registered before the measurement run, which method rule #3 asks for. Belly Drum swings Attack to +6 and so prices KO margins, which is where C27 argued the value is -- so the rank is plausibly higher than its one row suggests, but that is an assertion until computed.

19000093_51.STATUS: UNDETERMINED -- renderer or engine composition. The void mechanism is established; the cause of the segmentation failure is not.
19000093_51.confirmed: events.rs:766-779: when segment() returns None the branch is returned with ZERO components while the instruction list itself was OBSERVED complete and correct on replay -- an observation, not an established property, since the same entry allows that the pair-generated list may be an engine composition artifact (both hits, Showdown's order). Over 85% of the branch mass is voided this way.
19000093_51.v1s_named_candidate_is_REFUTED: v1 guessed the missing first-mover DecrementPP broke the split. It cannot: segment() does not read move markers at all. It re-runs generate_instructions_from_move per side and PREFIX-MATCHES the regenerated list against the full one (events.rs:410-412, :453-460, :478-490), so a marker absent from the engine's list is equally absent from the regeneration.
19000093_51.what_segmentation_failure_actually_means: the PAIR-generated instruction list is not reproducible by composing the two per-move generations. That is at least as plausibly an engine composition artifact as a renderer one.

disposition.note: v1 filed this RENDERER FIX / NOT an engine error with the predicate admittedly unpinned. The hedge was honest; the disposition on top of it was not.

19000093_53.confirmed: _ROLL_SCALED_SOURCES at engine_transition_differential.py:310-312 does not contain 'residual', so a residual component is exact-compared; move damage is source '' and gets roll tolerance. 55 vs 53 rejects in one bucket and passes in the other. That part of v1 holds.
19000093_53.v1s_cause_is_REFUTED: v1 said the missing move marker causes the segmenter to file Megahorn's damage as a residual, and prescribed emitting the marker consistently. segment() does not read markers (see 51 above), so the prescribed fix cannot work. The 'inconsistent emission' is also a deliberate commented engine rule, not an inconsistency: generate_instructions.rs:2800-2803 only decrements PP when the move is under 10 PP 'since that is when it starts to matter'. Hydro Pump (5) qualifies; Megahorn (10) and Rock Slide do not. SetLastUsedMove is separately gated on state.use_last_used_move (:2849), off in these states.
19000093_53.v1s_own_contrast_was_counter_evidence: v1 offered row 51 as showing the marker IS emitted elsewhere. Row 51 has the marker and is the row that fails segmentation outright; row 53 lacks it and segments fine. That is the opposite of the claimed correlation.

disposition.class: OPEN -- bucket effect understood, cause not

19000152_53.STATUS: CAUSED. Unchanged from v1 and independently confirmed by review.
19000152_53.cause: Perish Song kills with no damage message: base data/moves.ts onEnd emits |-start| perish0 then target.faint(), and faint() emits |faint| with no |-damage|. gen3 has no perishsong override; gen4's overrides only onResidualOrder. So Showdown's component set is empty for the faint while the engine renders capped_lethal=-132. Identical end states, different event vocabulary.
19000152_53.why_tolerance_does_not_save_it: capped_lethal IS roll-scaled, but with no observed counterpart this is a COUNT mismatch, not a magnitude one, so tolerance never applies.

disposition.detail: a |faint| with no preceding |-damage| must reconcile against an engine capped_lethal equal to the victim's remaining HP. Both sides are fully determined from source, so this is NOT a comparison limit.

tally.v1_said: 0 engine fixes, 3 renderer/matcher fixes, 1 comparison limit, and 'in none of them is the engine's simulation wrong'.
tally.why_that_was_wrong: it collapsed the two objectives the charter keeps apart. On 19000073/1 the per-roll simulation IS right and the engine is STILL at fault, because the fidelity objective is about whether the support contains every reachable sim transition, not about per-roll correctness. Written as v1 wrote it, the sentence is the exact reading the charter says will not surface that class of error.
tally.honest_position: one engine support gap, one caused matcher/renderer fix, two undetermined, and no comparison limits.

side_findings.c95_I5_hedge: v1 claimed to settle it by citing events.rs:751-765. That range is pre_ply_replacement, which does not gate the end-of-turn phase at all -- it is read by finish_ply to decide the |turn| line. The gating function is end_of_turn_triggered at :372-390. And 'extend the replacement predicate to the double-switch shape' as worded would suppress residuals on an ordinary VOLUNTARY double switch, which is a full turn and must keep its Leftovers. PR #1037 implemented a both-actives-fainted version and was still closed as a regression.
side_findings.c84: the contamination claim stands and is already applied on main via reports/c94. v1 stated it as though unaddressed.
